tools.name: check_ad_copy
tools.description: Checks Google responsive search ad or Meta ad text against character limits and common rejection reasons (symbols, capitals, repeated text, claims). Returns issues per line: fix (likely rejected or cut off) or look (worth a second look).

tools.name: daily_budget_max_spend
tools.description: The most Google Ads can charge in one day (2× the average daily budget) and in a month (30.4×) for a campaign daily budget.

tools.name: roas
tools.description: Return on ad spend from sales and ad spend, plus the break-even ROAS and profit for a profit margin.

tools.name: cpc
tools.description: Cost per click from spend and clicks, or clicks from spend and cost per click (any two of the three), plus CPM and click-through rate from impressions.

tools.name: google_ads_budget
tools.description: Monthly and daily Google Ads budget from a lead (or sales) goal: leads ÷ conversion rate = clicks, × cost per click = monthly budget, ÷ 30.4 = daily budget. Also the most Google can charge for that daily budget (2× a day, 30.4× a month) and a warning when it buys fewer than about 10 clicks a day.

tools.name: search_partners_cost
tools.description: Compares cost per conversion on Google Search with the Search Partners network and estimates what partners cost a month beyond Search, using the same rule as the SpendCanary scan.

tools.name: wasted_spend_from_search_terms
tools.description: Reads a Google Ads search terms report (CSV text) and totals the spend on search terms with no conversions, with the costliest ones and a monthly figure.

tools.name: check_landing_page
tools.description: Loads a public landing page on a phone and a computer and checks speed, redirects, a way to call, book or buy, and the Google tag. Limited to 5 checks an hour.

tools.name: google_ads_problem_trends
tools.description: How often each Google Ads wasted spend problem (junk searches, search partners, overspending, click fraud, location targeting, Google changing the account, PMax brand spend) comes up in public Reddit posts: the last 12 weeks, or monthly per 1,000 posts since January 2025.
